scenes.text: Astronauts can grow up to three percent taller in space.
On Earth, gravity is always squeezing your spine down.
In space, that pressure is gone, so the spine relaxes and stretches out.
For a person who is six feet tall, that can mean about two extra inches.
But it doesn't last, and their height goes back to normal after returning to Earth.
Would you go to space just to be taller for a while?

title: Astronauts get taller in space 🧑‍🚀
caption: Without gravity squeezing the spine, astronauts can grow up to 3% taller, about 2 inches (5 cm) for a 6-foot person. Back on Earth, they shrink back to normal!
